note: A control mapping is meaningful only against a known revision. Every source is pinned by SHA-256 or recorded as unresolved with the reason. An unresolved source is never silently substituted with a newer release. Source packages are not committed; only the generated Markdown under docs/srg/ is. Where a package has been rendered, the digest of the XCCDF actually rendered is recorded alongside the package digest, because that file is what the committed Markdown derives from.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 control catalogue, OSCAL JSON
sources.license: Not subject to copyright in the United States; see NIST usage terms
sources.notes: OSCAL 1.2.2. 20 families, 1196 controls and enhancements. Control identifiers resolve natively in OSCAL, which is why this is the spine rather than an SRG. Pinned at the oscal-content v1.5.0 tag rather than main, which moves; the bytes are those previously pinned from main. Release 5.2.0 (27 August 2025) added SA-15(13), SA-24, and SI-2(7) and revised SI-7(12); it exists only in OSCAL and NIST's online tools, as the published PDF is the 2020 text. The catalogue also carries the SP 800-53A assessment procedures: an assessment objective and examine, interview, and test methods for each control.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 HIGH baseline profile, OSCAL JSON
sources.license: Not subject to copyright in the United States; see NIST usage terms
sources.notes: Selects 370 controls: 188 base and 182 enhancements.

sources.title: Control Correlation Identifier (CCI) List
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Maps each CCI to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, which is what makes SRG-to-800-53 cross-references derivable: every SRG rule cites CCIs. Not rendered; it is an input to scripts/build-cci-crosswalk.py, and input records the digest of the XML that script reads. The URL carries no release, so DISA replaces the list in place; the weekly verification is what makes a replacement visible. 5137 items, 91 deprecated, 3838 Rev 5 references. Every CCI cited by the rendered Container Platform and GPOS SRGs resolves, is current, and carries a Rev 5 reference to a control present and not withdrawn in 800-53 5.2.0.

sources.title: Container Platform Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Governs the platform that runs containers rather than an image. 8 CAT I, 177 CAT II, 3 CAT III. Most of it is orchestrator-owned and will originate as host-inherited for any image component.

sources.title: General Purpose Operating System Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Per DoD guidance the GPOS SRG assesses image-level controls where no container-specific STIG exists. V3R4 removes V-203655 in favor of surviving V-278973 and rekeys V-278977 as V-282963. Group ID remains the rule-page key.

sources.publisher: Defense Information Systems Agency, for the Department of Defense
sources.title: Container Hardening Process Guide
sources.license: Distribution Statement A: approved for public release, distribution unlimited
sources.notes: Prose process guidance, not a rule catalogue, so it has no XCCDF and cannot be rendered by the SRG converter. The title is the one on the cover; the file is published as Final_DevSecOps_Enterprise_Container_Hardening_Guide_1.2.pdf, and an earlier revision of this register took its title from that filename. Much of it is Iron Bank and Platform One process. docs/standard/process-guide.md records where this standard follows it and where it departs.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: NIST SP 800-190, Application Container Security Guide
sources.license: Not subject to copyright in the United States; see NIST usage terms
sources.notes: The only NIST publication specific to container security, and the one the DISA Container Hardening Process Guide requires images to be consistent with (Appendix B). Its Section 4 countermeasures are mapped one by one in docs/standard/nist-800-190.md. Confirmed current on 2026-09-18: CSRC lists the September 2017 final with no revision or draft since. Its Appendix B maps container technologies to 800-53 Revision 4, not Revision 5, so it is cited but not joined to the spine.

sources.title: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Security Technical Implementation Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Host baseline, rendered as reference material. UBI filesystem applicability requires a separate per-rule decision; rendering does not transfer host checks to images. Removed rules do not waive controls. CAT I promotions and unmapped CCIs remain follow-ups in docs/ROADMAP.md.

sources.title: Web Server Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Applies to an image whose function is serving or proxying HTTP. It is the function-specific source for web servers and reverse proxies, and is selected per image by an applicability determination in that image's hardening profile. V4R5 repairs V-206372/V-206373 to CCI-003992 (CM-14). New and rekeyed rules require function-specific assessment.

sources.title: Application Server Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Applies to an image that hosts an application runtime and manages the applications deployed into it. Much of it presupposes a management interface, hosted applications, and user accounts, so an image with none of those can be determined not applicable against this revision, citing the rendered rules that presuppose them.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: NIST IR 8176, Security Assurance Requirements for Linux Application Container Deployments
sources.license: Not subject to copyright in the United States; see NIST usage terms
sources.notes: The companion to SP 800-190, below its threat model: host and kernel protection, namespaces, capabilities, images, registries, and orchestrators. No revision since.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.title: NIST SP 800-53A Revision 5, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls in Information Systems and Organizations
sources.license: Not subject to copyright in the United States; see NIST usage terms
sources.notes: Final January 2022. How each 800-53 control is assessed. The procedures this repository uses are read from the pinned OSCAL catalogue, which embeds them at release 5.2.0, including procedures for controls this PDF predates; the PDF is pinned as the published reference. No Revision 6 draft exists.

sources.title: Kubernetes Security Technical Implementation Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Benchmark date 01 Apr 2026. The product STIG instantiating the Container Platform SRG for Kubernetes. Probed V1R1 to V3R12 on 2026-09-18: V1R11 and V2R3 to V2R6 return 200, and V2R6 is the highest served. Pinned but not yet rendered.

sources.title: Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform 4.x Security Technical Implementation Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: The product STIG instantiating the Container Platform SRG for OpenShift. V2R7 keeps platform/host ownership: V-257564 concerns keystore encryption, and V-257580 concerns node audit rules. Rendering does not transfer these obligations to images.

sources.publisher: Defense Information Systems Agency, for the Department of Defense
sources.title: Container Image Creation and Deployment Guide
sources.license: Distribution Statement A: approved for public release, distribution unlimited
sources.notes: Version 2, Release 0.6 on the cover; the filename says 2.6. Rules for building and deploying images: non-privileged users, deterministic builds, trusted package sources, encrypted registry transport, minimal images. Filenames for 2.7, 2.8, 3.0, and 3.1 returned 404 on 2026-09-18.

sources.publisher: National Security Agency and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
sources.title: Kubernetes Hardening Guide
sources.license: US Government public release; may not be used to imply endorsement
sources.notes: Cybersecurity Technical Report U/OO/168286-21, PP-22-0324. The host's CDN refuses most automated clients with 403, so verification may report it unreachable; that says nothing about whether it changed. Retrieved once on 2026-09-18 with a browser's request headers, and the digest recorded then.

sources.title: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards
sources.license: CC BY 4.0
sources.notes: The Privileged, Baseline, and Restricted profiles. The rendered page cannot be pinned, so the source file is, at the kubernetes/website commit current on 2026-09-18. Restricted requires dropping every capability except NET_BIND_SERVICE, RuntimeDefault or Localhost seccomp, no privilege escalation, and a non-root user.

sources.title: OpenShift Container Platform: About security context constraints
sources.license: Apache-2.0
sources.notes: The documentation source for OpenShift's default SCCs, at the enterprise-4.22 branch commit current on 2026-09-18; docs.redhat.com refuses automated clients. restricted-v2 drops every capability, defaults seccomp to runtime/default, and forbids privilege escalation. restricted-v3, present from OpenShift 4.20, adds a required Linux user namespace (hostUsers: false). The documentation is inconsistent about which of the two new installations grant by default.

sources.title: Database Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Current DISA library entry checked 2026-11-08 (uploaded 2026-10-06). Conditional reference for postgresql-ubi, clickhouse-ubi, and neo4j-ubi as DBMSs without an applicable product-specific STIG. Vendor-specific Crunchy Data and EnterpriseDB STIGs are not automatically applicable to upstream PostgreSQL. SQL query/compute services do not become DBMSs merely by speaking SQL. 142 rules. Rendered after the 2026-11 DISA adoption restored the complete input set. See docs/applicability/application-functions.md.

sources.title: Application Programming Interface (API) Security Requirements Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Current final DISA library entry checked 2026-11-08 (uploaded 2025-11-25); not the earlier V1R0.1 draft. Conditional reference for lakekeeper-ubi, trino-ubi, and sail-ubi API services, and seaweedfs-ubi S3/administration APIs. Gateway, token, and HTTP-specific rules depend on the interface and deployment; an API client alone is not an API server. 65 rules. Rendered after the 2026-11 DISA adoption restored the complete input set. See docs/applicability/application-functions.md.

sources.title: Application Security and Development Security Technical Implementation Guide
sources.license: US Government work; redistribution terms stated in the package
sources.notes: Current DISA library entry checked 2026-11-08 (uploaded 2026-10-05). Nearest application-level reference for seaweedfs-ubi object storage and lakekeeper-ubi, trino-ubi, and sail-ubi application/compute behavior; its Overview section 1.1 covers network-connected enterprise applications, including RESTful services. No dedicated object-storage, Iceberg catalog, Trino, or Sail/Spark guide was found in the 417-entry public library. Storage Area Network STIG V2R5 is sunset and is not an object-storage baseline. This STIG does not supply object-store-specific or query-engine-specific configuration checks; development and operational requirements need their owning layer identified. 286 rules. Rendered after the 2026-11 DISA adoption restored the complete input set. See docs/applicability/application-functions.md.
